A1.justification: Both complete 39-page PDFs describe the same Conductor research. The main text, Appendices A–F, equations, tables, and figures are readable and matchable, with no material gaps preventing comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Conductor benchmark evaluations, worker-pool and recursion experiments, and ablation results in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the controlled benchmark comparisons in Table 7 and ablations in Tables 9–11.

M1.justification: The natural-language workflow specification, GRPO training, rewards, adaptive worker selection, and recursive inference are unchanged. The alternate topology variant in Appendix B.8 is also retained unchanged.

E1.justification: Both use the same MATH/MATH500, MMLU, RLPR, LiveCodeBench, AIME25, BigCodeBench, and GPQA-Diamond coverage. Appendix E retains the same Medreason, DeepMath, and Countdown few-shot sources.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across corresponding experiments: individual workers, consensus and reflection variants, MASRouter, MoA, RouterDC, Smoothie variants, and GPT-5/Gemini conductor replacements remain in Tables 5–11.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A retain the same splits, training budgets, model configurations, metrics, and testing procedures. Both preserve the unconstrained evaluation and the cost-constrained setting with 4096-token worker caps.

E4.justification: The model-scale, task-adaptivity, recursion, efficiency, and few-shot analyses are unchanged. Appendix B retains the same subtask, agent-selection, conductor-replacement, and topology ablations; Appendix F retains the same cases.

E5.justification: Both already specify up to 16 evaluation repetitions and reporting mean accuracy with standard errors in Section 4.1. Table 7 retains the same uncertainty reporting; no run-count or statistical-procedure changes appear.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative examples match. For example, Table 1 retains Conductor scores of 83.93 on LiveCodeBench and 87.5 on GPQA-Diamond, while Table 7 retains controlled LiveCodeBench accuracy of 64.29 ± 2.01.

T1.justification: The workflow definition, reward formulation, and GRPO objective and advantage equations in Sections 2–3 are identical. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about a 7B Conductor improving worker performance, learning coordination through RL, adapting to worker pools, and enabling recursive test-time scaling.

C2.justification: Interpretations of prompt engineering, worker specialization, task adaptivity, recursion, and OOD few-shot conditioning remain unchanged. The qualifications concerning costs and the limited benefits of fine-grained topologies are also retained.

D1.justification: Appendices A and E retain identical hyperparameters, hardware, preprocessing and evaluation details, prompts, and few-shot selection information. The reproducibility statement makes the same code and model-weight availability statements.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including Section 5. The first-page Liu and Brown citations receive formatting corrections without changing the referenced works or their role.

P1.justification: v2 adds the ICLR 2026 publication header, changes 'engineering efforts' to 'engineering effort,' and corrects introductory citation syntax. The remaining prose and section and appendix organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds a running publication header, updates the first-page arXiv stamp, and reflows the author lines. All 28 figures and 11 tables retain their content, captions, structure, and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 makes only small first-page editorial corrections and publication-format updates. The methods, empirical evidence, analyses, and reproducibility information remain identical, so the cosmetic refinements do not meaningfully change overall paper quality.
